title: Out of the Depths
summary: The Lord doesn't promise an easy path, but our hope is in his presence, his steadfast love and his redemption, as sure as the sunrise.
exhortation: It's true that as Christians we find ourselves in the depths, whether it's a darkness of soul, a season of personal suffering, or persecution from a fallen world. The Lord doesn't promise us an easy path. Quite the opposite. Yet the beauty of this psalm is that our hope is in his presence, his steadfast love and his redemption, and they are as sure to come as the sun is to rise.

So let's follow David's example in this psalm and put our hope in God, not only when everything is going well, but even more in the difficulties we are sure to face. Let's lift our eyes to our Savior Jesus, who loves us. His love is proven by his death on the cross, and his power to save is proven by his resurrection from the dead. And we find deep comfort in his promise that he will be with us always, to the end of the age.

If he clothes the lilies in such beauty, and his eye is on the smallest of creatures, he has not forgotten you. The infinite God of the universe is infinitely aware of you. He knows you better than you know yourself. Don't listen to the lie this morning that God isn't aware of you or is far from you. Sin is what keeps us far from God. If there is unrepentance, waywardness, or turning away from the Lord, turn back to him today. Don't delay another moment. Come back to the Lord and receive his mercy, forgiveness and kindness. He welcomes you back in.
prayer: Lord, set our eyes on you this morning, Jesus. Amen.
